claim: Laplacian/SR eigenoptions do not find bottleneck subgoals first. In the 4-room domain the fifth eigenoption is the first to end at a doorway, so the premise 'SR eigenvectors find bottleneck subgoals' is only partly right (a normalised-cut sign partition can; individual eigenoptions do not).
agent_test: Compare a subgoal library seeded by bottleneck detection against one seeded by structure-spanning subgoals on the same tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Bottleneck-only options can make exploration worse (diffusion time rises in 4-room) while eigenoptions with enough options cut it; bottleneck options stay competitive when the goal sits near a doorway.
agent_test: On tasks with the goal near vs far from a chokepoint, compare bottleneck-subgoal vs spanning-subgoal decompositions.

claim: A random-subgoal control fails: random options mostly raise diffusion time by orders of magnitude, so eigenoptions beat arbitrary option sets.
agent_test: Always include a random-subgoal control arm when testing any learned subgoal library.

claim: Eigenoptions speed up tabular Q-learning with as few as four options and never hurt in ten sampled four-room tasks; the best result in the original paper used 64.
agent_test: Cap the subgoal library small (about 4) and test whether a small set already gives most of the gain.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Covering options (Jinnai 2019) beat eigenoptions in their own study (six domains) but gave no gain in Machado 2023's ten four-room tasks and were brittle with an online SR. The rival-rule ranking is unsettled.
agent_test: Do not assume one discovery rule; run two rules head to head on our task mix.

claim: The eigenoption idea extends to pixels and online learning (deep SR 2018, DCEO 2023), but results are mixed: 3 of 4 Atari games worked, Freeway failed, Montezuma subgoals were found qualitatively, and RND at 2B steps passed DCEO at 200M steps.
agent_test: Not testable on a text agent; a caution that graph-spectral discovery needs a state graph we do not have.

claim: Choosing the best option set for planning is NP-hard (log n inapproximable in deterministic MDPs), so every discovery rule is a heuristic.
agent_test: None; justification for keeping the library small and revisable.

claim: Most of the benefit of hierarchy in RL comes from better exploration, not easier policy learning; a flat agent trained on the hierarchical agent's data is nearly as good.
agent_test: Test whether a subgoal library helps by diversifying what is tried or by structuring the final solution: compare library-as-explorer vs library-as-plan.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: People pick graph bottlenecks as subgoals: bottlenecks chosen first 4.4x as often as other locations (N=40), recognised faster (98% accuracy), Tower of Hanoi preference (N=35). A Bayesian partition model reproduces this and predicts new biases (Tomov 2020: 58/87, p=0.003; 53/78 vs control chi2=6.52, p=0.01).
agent_test: Check whether our agent's chosen subgoals in graph-like puzzles land on bottleneck states more than chance.

claim: Human segmentation follows community structure even when local transition statistics are equal (Schapiro 2013: t(29)=2.27; fMRI N=20 pattern similarity within community).
agent_test: Test if community-aware segmentation of a long trace improves summary quality at equal tokens.

claim: Humans show a pseudo-reward prediction error for subgoal progress, separate from final-goal progress (EEG N=9; fMRI dorsal ACC N=30; accumbens N=14). Small samples, one task.
agent_test: Give the agent an explicit subgoal-progress check separate from the overall goal check; compare to a single check.

claim: Humans learn reusable options and show negative transfer when the old option no longer fits (Xia & Collins n=25+55; Li & Collins N=1026 replicates Block 7). First-stage MTurk negative transfer did not replicate, and a meta-learning model fit better than a fully hierarchical one.
agent_test: Add a stale-subgoal test: reuse a stored subgoal on a changed task, measure the damage, and test an invalidation rule.

claim: Human revaluation is partly SR-like: reward revaluation is easier than transition revaluation (n=58: .52 vs .45; MTurk n=88: .66 vs .47), best fit by an SR plus model-based hybrid. Support for SR as the mechanism is moderate.
agent_test: Not directly testable; background only.

claim: Frontier LLMs plan poorly on graph structure: edges listed well but shortest path to a state one cluster away succeeded 0 of 30 for GPT-4 at temperature 0 and at most 10% at others; BFS/DFS instructions help inconsistently.
agent_test: Test whether handing the agent an explicit graph of the problem (nodes, clusters) beats free recall at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: Re-read: GPT-4 0/30 at temperature 0 and at most 10% at 0.5 or 1; no reasoning-model or graph-tool test found (gap 6 open).

claim: PlanBench: GPT-4 solved 34.3% of Blocksworld plan-generation instances (206/600), so decomposition has headroom on classical planning.
agent_test: Use Blocksworld-style tasks as a decomposition test bed.

claim: Subgoal search with a learned subgoal generator beats low-level search: Rubik's cube near 100% vs under 10%; Sokoban 12x12 0.66 vs 0.15 and 20x20 0.46 vs 0.02; about 65% of subgoals reduce distance and 17% increase it. Subgoal distance has a sweet spot (k=3 INT, k=4 cube).
agent_test: Vary subgoal granularity (steps between subgoals) and look for a sweet spot at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Decomposing only when the executor fails (ADaPT) beats ReAct, plan-and-execute, retry and Reflexion on GPT-3.5: ALFWorld 71.6 vs 43.3/43.3/47.8/57.5; WebShop 44.0 vs 32.0; TextCraft 52.0 vs 19.0. Corrected: the headline 28.3 points is over ReAct and Plan-and-Execute; over Reflexion it is 14.1. Compute is not matched across arms.
agent_test: Implement as-needed decomposition (split only on failure) and compare to always-decompose at equal tokens.
gap_search_note: ADaPT matched LLM calls, not tokens, vs Try-Again and Reflexion; no always-decompose arm and no frontier-model comparison. Select-Then-Decompose shows explicit decomposition costs 4-10x tokens with no gain on GSM8K. Status stays single-source for the ADaPT result; gap 2 open.

claim: Up-front plan-then-solve prompting (least-to-most) gives big gains on tasks longer than the examples (SCAN length 99.7% vs 16.2%; last-letter length 12: 74.0 vs 31.8) but small gains on GSM8K (62.39 vs 60.97; 45.23 vs 39.07 for 5+ steps).
agent_test: Test decomposition on tasks beyond the model's usual horizon and verify it does not hurt short tasks.

claim: Subgoals in demonstrations or proposed by an LLM help downstream (miniF2F 38.9 to 44.3%; DLLM +27.7% HomeGrid, +21.1% Crafter, +9.9% Minecraft), but zero-shot LLM judging of subgoal reach on NetHack is weak (Llama-3-70B F1 0.16 in one table) and ELLM goal conditioning gave no significant pretraining gain.
agent_test: Measure how reliably the agent itself judges 'subgoal reached' before using that signal for control.
gap_search_note: Whole-trajectory LLM judges max 70% precision (AgentRewardBench); subgoal-level verifier arm still unmeasured (gap 4 open).

claim: A verified, retrievable skill library compounds: Voyager 3.3x more unique items; removing self-verification cut items 73%. Library value depends on verification, not size.
agent_test: Add a verification gate before a subgoal or procedure enters memory; ablate it.
gap_search_note: Verification and lifecycle tracking support library value, but all from RL-trained policies; still not replicated for prompt-only agents.

claim: Discovering skills by compression: LLM segmentation plus an MDL term gives BabyAI zero-shot 43 vs 34 for behaviour cloning; removing the MDL term lowers performance.
agent_test: Prefer subgoals that shorten the description of many past solutions; compare to frequency-only selection.

claim: Automatic subgoal discovery from LLM reasoning traces exists and works: label each step of correct ReAct traces, merge into 5-10 move categories, rank by frequency, run the top few as separate sub-calls (ARISE). Five-task mean 67.4 vs ReAct 38.8 (DeepSeek-V3) and 77.7 vs 68.2 (Gemini 2.5 Flash). No study compares it with hand-written decomposition at matched tokens.
agent_test: Mine move categories from the agent's own solved traces; compare with a hand-written subgoal list at equal total tokens.

claim: Induced subgoal text helps mainly when executed as a separate LLM call. As in-context skill text on Gemini 2.5 Flash it scored 66.1 (below ReAct 68.2); as subroutines 77.7. Removing the induced content but keeping the interface cut accuracy from 78.4 to 67.7.
agent_test: Run each subgoal as an isolated call with only its spec and inputs; ablate against the same text placed in the main prompt.

claim: Library size for language subgoals: 3 to 5 active entries is enough and larger is not better. ARISE K=3/5/10 on DeepSeek-V3: K=10 never best (object 51.9 at K=10 vs 71.7 at K=3). Adding 1,000 irrelevant skills cut loaded-skill recall from 73.6% to 27.4% and raised the zero-load rate from 9.3% to 51.6%; explicit selection kept 73.9% recall.
agent_test: Cap the active subgoal set near 5 and pre-select with an explicit step, not agent scanning.

claim: Stored reasoning memories go stale and vote counters (ExpeL/ACE style) are slow to notice: 7.0 to 13.5 times more stale answers than a certified rule on five LLMs, 35 to 73 times on code with an exact test. A likelihood-ratio detector plus an edit notice or restart cut stale answers to 0 (perfect notices) from 946-967 per 10^4 queries. Not yet shown for subgoal libraries, and not independently replicated.
agent_test: Store each subgoal with a re-runnable check and a version tag; retire on check failure, not on vote counts.

claim: Explicit decomposition costs far more tokens than it earns on easy reasoning: GSM8K CoT 93.17% at 396 tokens vs Plan-and-Execute 92.34% at 2,443; a selector that chooses per task reached 93.56% at 517 tokens. Execution model size matters more than decomposition model size.
agent_test: Gate decomposition on a difficulty check and compare against always-decompose at equal tokens.

claim: Clustering trajectories into skills can give readable but useless libraries: 5 of 8 clusters had purity at least 0.95, yet downstream skill-step accuracy rose only 18.5 to 20.5% and a frequency baseline beat the generated skill file at every training size. Judge reliability is also limited: no LLM judge exceeded 70% precision on web-agent success.
agent_test: Always include a frequency-prior baseline and an executable check when scoring discovered subgoals.
